Where it began

Tillakaratne Dilshan was born in Kalutara on 14 October 1976. He began playing cricket in his teens at Kalutara Vidyalaya, and cricket ran in the family: his brother, Tillakaratne Sampath, went on to play first-class cricket in Sri Lanka.

He made his Test and one-day debuts in Zimbabwe in 1999. His first Test innings, at Bulawayo, brought 9 runs. In the next Test, at Harare, he made an unbeaten 163 and was player of the match as Sri Lanka won.

The player

Dilshan played 87 Tests for Sri Lanka between 1999 and 2013. He scored 5,492 runs at 40.99, with 16 hundreds, 23 fifties and a best of 193 at Lord's, then the highest by a Sri Lankan there. He also took 39 wickets with his off-breaks and held 79 catches, plus 9 more as wicketkeeper. In his 50th Test he made a hundred in each innings.

For years he batted at six or seven and was rather overlooked. Then he was moved up to open, and everything changed. He was the leading run-scorer at the 2011 World Cup, with 500 runs, including a hundred against England in the quarter-final. He passed 10,000 one-day runs and won the World Twenty20 in 2014. After the 2011 World Cup he captained Sri Lanka in all three formats, leading them in 11 Tests, and under him they won a Test in South Africa for the first time.

What made him special

He was an attacking right-hander full of ideas. During the 2009 IPL he came up with a shot that flicked the ball over the wicketkeeper's head, and it soon became known as the Dilscoop. That year he was player of the tournament at the World Twenty20, and his 96 not out against West Indies in the semi-final won an ICC award. He was also the first player to score hundreds in all three formats while captain.

Age barely slowed him. In 2015, the year he turned 39, he made 1,207 one-day runs, and his hundred against Scotland at that year's World Cup made him, at the time, its oldest centurion. With the ball he was a handy part-timer rather than a match-winner, though his 4 for 10 in a Test shows what he could do on a good day.

Away from the middle

A popular figure at home, he tried acting on television from 2017 and judged Sri Lanka's Got Talent. He also released music videos and lent the Dil Scoop name to a fashion line.

Retirement did not keep him off the field for long. In the 2020–21 Road Safety World Series he captained Sri Lanka Legends and was player of the series, top of both the run and wicket lists with 271 runs and 12 wickets.

And finally

In his last Twenty20 international, against Australia in September 2016, he made a single run. Then he took the ball and picked up two late wickets, one of them with the very last ball he bowled for his country. Not many players write their own ending so neatly.
